title: Add frontend component and page tests
description:
Create `dashboard/frontend/__tests__/landing/LandingPage.test.tsx`.

Tests:
1. **Grid layout**: render EditorialGrid, verify CSS grid template columns are '260px 1fr 320px'.
2. **DefinePanel rendering**: render with mock data. Verify vision warning appears for 'missing' status. Verify draft spec items rendered. Verify defect severity badges.
3. **JudgePanel rendering**: render with pending review mock data. Verify hero metrics (coverage, criteria, verdict, decisions). Verify CTA button text. Mock `useRouter` and verify push to `/outcome-review?feature=X` on CTA click.
4. **ExecutePanel rendering**: render with running features and escalation. Verify progress bar widths. Type in escalation input, click Send, verify `onRespondToEscalation` called with correct args.
5. **LearnPanel rendering**: render with coverage trend, insights, escalation trend. Verify sorted order. Verify good/warn indicators.
6. **Empty states**: render each panel with empty arrays. Verify no crash, empty state messages shown.
7. **Page integration**: mock the GraphQL query hook to return fixture data. Render `page.tsx`. Verify all four panels present. Verify loading skeleton shown initially.

Use the project's existing test framework (Jest + React Testing Library based on Next.js convention).

spec_references.requirement: Frontend tests: grid layout snapshot, panel rendering, escalation input, CTA routing, empty states, subscription integration
Items 10-12: T-shape grid, inline escalation, CTA routing

rationale: Frontend tests are the final verification layer, depending on all components and the page being assembled. A single test file covers all panels because the tests share mock data fixtures and the page integration test needs all components present.
assumptions: Project uses Jest + React Testing Library (standard Next.js test setup)
CSS grid template values can be tested via computed styles or snapshot testing
decisions: Added `gql` to the urql mock factory so mission-control.ts can initialize its query constant at module load time without throwing.
Used distinct feature names in coverageTrend vs escalationTrend fixtures to prevent getAllByText collisions in the sort-order test.
Rendered real child components in the page integration tests rather than mocking them — urql is the only thing that needs mocking since the components themselves don't use it.
Used `…` (unicode ellipsis U+2026) in getByPlaceholderText to match the literal character in ExecutePanel.tsx:116 rather than three separate dots.
Used Array.from + .find on querySelectorAll('div[style]') for the progress bar width test — cannot add data-testid to ExecutePanel (owned by task 13).
concerns: 4 pre-existing failures in JudgePanel.test.tsx (task 12) and app/page.test.tsx (task 17) exist on the branch — not caused by or fixable by this task.

toHaveStyle with CSS variable tokens (var(--color-green), var(--color-amber)) follows the pattern established by LearnPanel.test.tsx; if JSDOM's CSS variable support regresses, these assertions would need to switch to toHaveAttribute('style', ...).
